observation.visible_scene: A wide beach at sunset: a colorful sky with orange, yellow and teal clouds over a glowing sun near the horizon, a flat ocean with a line of breaking waves, and a broad sheet of wet sand in the foreground that mirrors the sky's colors (gold on the left, turquoise on the right). The framing is a static landscape shot; no people, animals or objects are present.
visible_changes: The breaking-wave foam crest in the mid-distance shifts and reshapes slowly across the segment, advancing and retreating a little relative to the horizon line.
The thinner wash/foam line closer to the shore changes its position and texture frame to frame, consistent with a slow, ongoing wave cycle rather than a start or stop.
Small ripples and the boundary of the reflected water film on the wet sand subtly move, altering the shimmer of the gold/turquoise reflection.
The sky, cloud shapes, sun glow and horizon line remain essentially fixed in position throughout the excerpt.
The camera viewpoint is static: the horizon and cloud features do not translate across the frame, so the observed motion belongs to the water, not to camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the wave motion continues, reverses or completes a cycle beyond this ~2.7 s window.
The exact tidal state or wind driving the waves (not visible).
Any events before t=0 or after the last frame; both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: The precise direction and magnitude of the foam-line movement is hard to read at this frame rate; only that the wave/foam pattern is continuously changing is well supported.
Distinguishing the thin receding wash on the sand from a separate incoming wave is not fully resolvable.
Tiny apparent shifts in the reflection cannot be confirmed as real water motion versus compression artifacts.
